answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a stake-backed kernel: each agent locks a deposit that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. A public beacon publishes a random audit seed each round, and a random subset of agents must prove recent useful work to keep their standing; failures forfeit stake. New identities start with a lotus-like trust score that grows only slowly through verified work, so fresh Sybils cannot immediately wield influence.
